species.real: The name means what it says: it lives in hedges and grunts like a pig while it hunts.
species.name: Spikkin

dex.text: Snuffles along hedge bottoms at dusk, grumbling to itself. Rolls into a prickly ball and waits for trouble to get bored.
dex.fact: A hedgehog has around 5,000 to 7,000 spines. Each one is a hollow hair made stiff with keratin, the same stuff as your fingernails.

species.real: Hedgehogs sometimes chew something strong-smelling into a froth and lick it all over their spines. It is called self-anointing, and nobody is sure why they do it.
species.name: Bramblehog

dex.text: Its spines have grown into living bramble. Gardeners leave a gap under the fence for it, which it considers the least they could do.
dex.fact: Hedgehogs can travel a mile or more a night looking for food, which is why holes in garden fences, called hedgehog highways, help them so much.

species.real: Hedgehogs are lactose intolerant, so the traditional saucer of milk gives them an upset stomach; meaty cat food and a dish of water are what they actually want.
species.name: Thornsow

dex.text: A walking hedgerow the size of a pony. Old farmers say a field with a Thornsow in it never needs a gate.
dex.fact: Hedgehogs are one of the few mammals with some resistance to adder venom, though they are not immune.
